                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>
                     </ns0:hi> to you to be a true Apostle.) Amongst these, he reckons 1. <ns0:hi>Patience.</ns0:hi> 2. <ns0:hi>Mi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />racles.</ns0:hi> The first refers to those many labours which he had, in travelling to propagate the Gospel, in Preaching, Writing, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> this manifested him called of God to the work. 2. <ns0:hi>Miraculous operations</ns0:hi> were another sign; for though the working of Mira<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cles was not restrained to the Apostolical Office, yet when they were wrought in confirmation of the Doctrine which the Apostle had first preached, and so were a Seal of his Ministry, they were truly signs of his Apostleship: it being no way probable, that the God of truth, would have communicated his power to men for the confirmation of lies, or of an employment to which he had never called them.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="13">13 For what is it wherein ye were inferiour to other Churches, except <ns0:hi>it be</ns0:hi> that <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 11.9.</ns0:note> I my self was not burdensome to you <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">Wherein have not you been used as any other Gospel-Churches were, where <ns0:hi>Peter,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Iames,</ns0:hi> or any other of the Apostles have laboured? Hath not the same Doctrine been preached to you? Have not as great Miracles been wrought a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mongst you? Hath not the Holy Ghost been as plentifully shed abroad amongst you, to inrich you with all spiritual Gifts? So as you have come behind in no Gospel benefit. I know of no<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thing in which it hath not fared with you as with other Church<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />es, except in this; that whereas in other Churches the Apostles or their Pastors, have been burdensome to them, taking <ns0:hi>Stipends</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Salaries</ns0:hi> for their pains; I have forborn it and have not at all charged you. If this be a <ns0:hi>wrong</ns0:hi> to you, I hope it is not of that nature, but I may obtain of you a pardon for it. The rea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sons of the Apostles thus sparing the Church of <ns0:hi>Corinth</ns0:hi> more than some other Churches, we have before guessed at.</ns0:note>? Forgive me this wrong.</ns0:p>

                  </ns0:note> for you <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">I am so far from desiring your money, that if I had it, I would willingly spend it for you; and I do spend my strength for you, willing to die in your service, labouring for the good of your immortal Souls.</ns0:note>, though the <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 6.12, <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> more abundantly I love you, the less I be loved <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">But I am very unhappy as to some of you, who will not rightly understand me, but love me the less, the more they see my love to them.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="16">16 But be it so: I did not burden you: never<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />theless, being crafty, I caught you with guile <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">I hear what some say, It is true, that when I was my self with you, I laid no burden upon you, did not put you upon any Collection for me; but, like a crafty man, I set others to take money of you for my use. So as, what I did not by my self, I did by those whom I imployed. This appeareth to be the sense by what followeth in the next verse, where he appeal<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth to them for his vindication in this particular.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="17">17 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 7.2.</ns0:note> Did I make a gain of you by any of them, whom I sent unto you?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="18">18 I desired Titus <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">The Apostle, to avoid or wipe off this imputation, appeal<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth to themselves, to name any person (whom he had sent un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />to them) that had taken any thing of them for his use. He saith, that he desired <ns0:hi>Titus</ns0:hi> to come to them, of this desire we read before <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 8.6, 16, 18, 22.</ns0:note>, and with <ns0:hi>him</ns0:hi> I sent a bro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">With him (he saith) he sent <ns0:hi>another Brother</ns0:hi>; this is that Brother, of whom he had said, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 18. <ns0:hi>That his praise was in the Gospel throughout all the Churches.</ns0:hi> Some guess it was <ns0:hi>Luke,</ns0:hi> but there is no certainty of that; he appeals to them, whether either of these made <ns0:hi>a gain of them?</ns0:hi> that is, took any thing of them.</ns0:note>: Did Titus make a gain of you? walked we not in the same spirit? <ns0:hi>walked we</ns0:hi> not in the same steps <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">And whether they did not walk <ns0:hi>in the same spirit, and in the same steps?</ns0:hi> Whe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther they did not shew the same generosity and freedom? And by their behaviour amongst them did not shew, that they did not seek what was <ns0:hi>theirs</ns0:hi> (to be inriched, by their Estates) <ns0:hi>but them</ns0:hi>; to communicate the riches of Grace to their Souls. The circumstances of Gods Providence may be such towards faithful Ministers, as that they may be constrained to make use of others to do their work; but such, so near as they can judge, will never make use of any therein, but such as are of the <ns0:hi>same Spirit</ns0:hi> with themselves, and walk in the <ns0:hi>same steps.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="19">19 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 5.12<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>
                  </ns0:note> Again, think you that we excuse our selves unto you <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">Some of you may think, that I speak all this in my own defence, and seek only my own credit and reputation amongst you. I do not so,</ns0:note>? We speak before God in Christ <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">I speak as a Christian, as one who knows that God knoweth, seeth, and observeth what I say; searching my heart, and trying my reins.</ns0:note>: but <ns0:hi>we do</ns0:hi> all things, dearly beloved, for your edify<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">All that I say I speak for your good, that you may be built up in Faith, and Love, and all other Graces: A great hinderance to which, is prejudice against me, and such as are the Ministers of the Gospel to you; which I therefore desire (what in me lieth) to prevent and obviate. The Apostle, not only here, but in several other parts of these, and other his Epistles, declares what ought to be the great end of his, and all other Ministers, <ns0:hi>viz.</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Edification of people.</ns0:hi> The Conversion of the Unconverted, and the perfecting of those in whom the foundation is laid, building them up in all good spiritual habits; both of these come under the notion of <ns0:hi>Edifi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cation.</ns0:hi> If we consider Christ as the Foundation, <ns0:hi>Conversion</ns0:hi> is <ns0:hi>Edification</ns0:hi>; the building up of Souls upon Christ, who is the Gospel foundation; and <ns0:hi>other foundation can no man lay.</ns0:hi> If we consider the infusion of the first habits of Grace into the Soul, as the <ns0:hi>Foundation, Edification</ns0:hi> signifies a going on from Faith to Faith, a growing in Grace and in the knowledge of the Lord Jesus Christ, a going on to perfection. The true Minister of Christ ought to make <ns0:hi>Edification</ns0:hi> in both of these senses his end and his great end; for by this means is God glorified, the Souls of his people benefited, and eternally saved.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="20">20 For I fear, lest when I come, I shall not find you such as I would <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">A good man, especially a faithful Minister of the Gospel, will be concerned at the sins of others, and as to their spiritual welfare. A profane person, either rejoyceth in the sins of o<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thers, or at least is unconcerned for them; but a good man can<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />not be so; as knowing the sins of others reflect dishonour up<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on God.</ns0:note>, and <ns0:hi>that</ns0:hi> 
                  <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Cor. 4.21. Chap. 10.2. & 13.2, 10.</ns0:note> I shall be found unto you such as ye would not <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">He also cannot delight in the punishments of others, or doing any thing which may be ingrateful to them. <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi> fear<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth lest the miscarriages of this Church should inforce from him some acts of <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>everity.</ns0:note>, lest <ns0:hi>there be</ns0:hi> de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bates <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">He instanceth in some particular disor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ders in the members of this Church, which he feared that he should find amongst them not amended; all the effects of Pride, and Passion.</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">Debates, or contentions, such as he had taxed them for, 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 1.11. and 3.3.</ns0:note>, envyings <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">Envyings, or heats of Passion; Envying of one another for their gifts, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> The o<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther things which he mentioneth, are all sins against that Bro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />therly love which ought to be found amongst Christians, and tending to ruptures amongst them; and teach us how contrary these are to the duty of Christians, who are one body.</ns0:note>, wraths, strifes, back-bitings, whisperings, swellings, tumults.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="21">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:473" />21 <ns0:hi>And</ns0:hi> lest, when I come again, my God will humble me among you, and that I shall bewail many which have sinned already, and have not re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pented of the uncleanness, and fornication, and lasciviousness which they have committed <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">From hence it appeareth, that this Church of <ns0:hi>Corinth,</ns0:hi> (though it had many in it, without doubt, who were true and sincere Christians, yet) had also many in it which were other<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />wise; yea, many that were scandalous; (for such are those mentioned in this Verse.) Again, the Apostles mentioning of <ns0:hi>many</ns0:hi> that had committed <ns0:hi>Vncleanness, Fornication,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Lasci<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />viousness,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>not repented</ns0:hi>; whenas he had only given order for the Excommunication of one incestuous person, 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 5. and in this Epistle, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 7. had given order for the restoring him upon his repentance; lets us know, that the Governours of Churches ought to use a great deal of <ns0:hi>Prudence</ns0:hi> in the admi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nistring of Church-censures. We are also further taught, That nothing more afflicteth a godly person, who hath the charge of the Souls of others, than to see them go on in courses of sin without repentance. Whether <ns0:hi>bewailing,</ns0:hi> in this Verse, im<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />plieth proceeding to <ns0:hi>Ecclesiastical Censures,</ns0:hi> (as several Interpre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ters think) I doubt; for as the word doth not necessarily imply <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t, so his sparing use of <ns0:hi>that Rod,</ns0:hi> which he could (though absent) have as well used against other unclean persons as one incestuous person; and chusing rather that the Sentence should be decla<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />red against him by the Church in his absence, than by himself when present; inclineth me to think, that by <ns0:hi>bewailing</ns0:hi> here, he only means a Christian afflictive sense of their miscarriages; whereas his desire was, that he might have a chearful comfort<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />able journey to, and abode with them. But yet, in the next Chapter, he seemeth to threaten something more against some particular offenders.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
